faqs.q: What is the number one golf course in Vietnam?
faqs.a: Hoiana Shores Golf Club, designed by Robert Trent Jones Jr. on the Central Coast near Hoi An, is consistently Vietnam's top-ranked course by Asia Pacific Golf, Top 100 Golf Courses, and the AGS expert panel. Its links setting, conditioning quality, and dramatic finish along the East Sea coastline make it Vietnam's premier layout.

faqs.q: Which golf region in Vietnam has the best courses?
faqs.a: Da Nang and the Central Coast (Hoi An, Quảng Nam) has the highest concentration of top-tier courses in Vietnam. Four of our top 10 are within 45 minutes of each other in this region. Ho Chi Minh City and Ho Tram contribute the Bluffs and Vietnam Golf & Country Club to the national ranking.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to play the top golf courses in Vietnam?
faqs.a: Green fees at Vietnam's top-10 courses typically range from USD $150 (mid-tier) to ~$300 USD (Hoiana Shores, Bluffs Ho Tram) per round. AGS packages include all green fees, caddie fees, private transfers, and accommodation as part of fully bespoke itineraries.

faqs.q: Do all top Vietnam golf courses have caddie service?
faqs.a: Yes — caddies are mandatory at all of Vietnam's premier courses and are included in every AGS Vietnam itinerary. Caddie quality varies; AGS maintains relationships with head caddies at each property to ensure our clients receive consistently excellent service.

faqs.q: Is Vietnam golf worth it for Australian golfers?
faqs.a: Absolutely — and it's among the best value premium golf experiences available to Australians. Green fees, accommodation, and dining at Vietnam's finest properties cost significantly less than equivalent Japanese or UK golf, with course quality that is genuinely comparable. Flight times from major Australian capitals to Da Nang (via Singapore or Bangkok) are approximately 10–12 hours.

faqs.q: What are the main updates to Vietnam golf courses in 2026?
faqs.a: Several top tier courses in Da Nang and Ho Tram have undergone extensive bunker renovations and green resurfacing to maintain their world-class status for the 2026 season.

faqs.q: Are caddies mandatory at these top 10 courses?
faqs.a: Yes, in Vietnam, a highly trained caddie is mandatory at almost all championship courses. Their green-reading skills are essential for the complex coastal breaks.

Executive Summary:

  • Hoiana Shores Golf Club (Quảng Nam, Par 71, Robert Trent Jones Jr. design) is ranked #1 for 2026, noted as a links masterpiece with a back nine along the East Sea coast, recommended for both first and last plays on any Da Nang circuit.
  • The Bluffs Ho Tram Strip (Ba Ria-Vung Tau, Par 71, Greg Norman design) is ranked #2, distinguished as Vietnam's only clifftop course with its back nine 30 meters above the South China Sea, and considered Norman's finest Asian design.
  • Ba Na Hills Golf Club (Da Nang, Par 72, Luke Donald design) secures the #3 spot, offering mountain golf at 1,500m elevation with a unique night golf option, providing a remarkable contrast to coastal courses.
  • Montgomerie Links Vietnam (Da Nang, Par 72, Colin Montgomerie design) is ranked #4, offering Scotland-influenced links golf on the Central Coast, characterized as tactical and wind-affected, appealing to strategic players.

Vietnam's golf industry has evolved rapidly over the past decade. From a handful of colonial-era resort courses to a national portfolio of 80+ layouts — including work from Robert Trent Jones Jr., Greg Norman, Nick Faldo, Luke Donald, and Colin Montgomerie — the country now offers a genuine world-class golf circuit.

These are the 10 courses that Asia Golf Specialists considers essential for any serious golf traveller to Vietnam in 2026. Rankings are based on our direct experience over multiple years, client feedback, and assessment across course design, conditioning, caddie quality, and overall experience.

1. Hoiana Shores Golf Club

Designer: Robert Trent Jones Jr. | Location: Quảng Nam | Par: 71 | Rating: ★★★★★

Vietnam's undisputed finest. A links masterpiece on natural duneland, with a back nine that plays along the East Sea coast. The course we recommend playing first and last on any Da Nang circuit. Read our full Hoiana Shores review.

2. The Bluffs Ho Tram Strip

Designer: Greg Norman | Location: Ba Ria-Vung Tau | Par: 71 | Rating: ★★★★★

The only clifftop course in Vietnam. Norman's finest Asian design, with the back nine running along the South China Sea ridgeline 30 metres above the waves. Norman's personal favourite in the region. Full review: Bluffs Ho Tram.

3. Ba Na Hills Golf Club

Designer: Luke Donald | Location: Da Nang | Par: 72 | Rating: ★★★★★

Mountain golf at 1,500m elevation with an unmissable night golf option. The contrast between the Da Nang coastal courses and Ba Na Hills' highland setting is genuinely remarkable. Full review: Ba Na Hills review.

4. Montgomerie Links Vietnam

Designer: Colin Montgomerie | Location: Da Nang | Par: 72 | Rating: ★★★★☆

Scotland-influenced links golf on the Central Coast. Tactical, wind-affected, and more unforgiving than the long yardage suggests. The thinking player's choice in the Da Nang circuit.

5. BRG Đà Nẵng Golf Resort (Norman Course)

Designer: Greg Norman | Location: Da Nang | Par: 72 | Rating: ★★★★☆

Da Nang's most established course — the former Danang Golf Club redesigned into a 36-hole facility. Wide fairways, excellent conditioning, and an accessible challenge for mid-handicappers. A strong third-day option in a Da Nang circuit.

6–10: The Supporting Circuit

6. Vinpearl Golf Nam Hội An

Schmidt-Curley design — 27 holes, strong conditioning, competitive tee fees. Good 4th course in a Da Nang extension.

7. Laguna Golf Lăng Cô

Sir Nick Faldo's only Vietnam design — mountain-meets-coast layout with the Trường Sơn mountains as a backdrop. Spectacular scenery.

8. Vietnam Golf & Country Club (Ho Chi Minh City)

The original prestige address in Southern Vietnam. Twin 18-hole layouts, immaculate conditioning, and a membership roster that reads like a corporate directory.

9. Dalat Palace Golf Club

Vietnam's most atmospheric course — a 1920s French-era layout at 1,500m in the Đà Lạt highlands. Colonial character and cool mountain temperatures year-round.

10. Kings Island Golf Resort (Hanoi)

Northern Vietnam's finest — Robert Trent Jones Jr. on a river island outside Hanoi. The island setting and mountain backdrop make this a standout experience for golfers combining Hanoi culture with golf.
